parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The Moon may be considered to be a uniform sphere with a diameter of $3.5 \times 10^{3}$ km and a
mass of $7.4 \times 10^{22}\,\mathrm{kg}$.
A meteor strikes the Moon and, during the collision, a rock is sent off from the surface of the
Moon with an initial speed v.
Assuming that the Moon is isolated in space, determine the minimum speed of the rock such
that it does not return to the Moon’s surface. Explain your working.
$minimum speed = m s ^{1} $

markscheme_points.text: initial kinetic energy = (-) potential energy (at surface) or ½mv2 = GMm / r

hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in A Level Physics theory and principles connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
parts.proper_answer: initial kinetic energy = (-) potential energy (at surface) or ½mv2 = GMm / r; v2 = (2 × 6.67 × 10-11 × 7.4 × 1022) / (0.5 × 3.5 × 106); v = 2.4 × 103 m s-1
